issues.title: Fix DS/DSi compatibility, Wi-Fi power saving and JIT invalidation
issues.body:
This fixes DS/DSi register handling, Wi-Fi power saving and JIT literal invalidation, and avoids redundant renderer work.

- **DS/DSi compatibility:** apply the appropriate SCFG register initialization and access restrictions when running DS software in DSi mode.
- **Wi-Fi:** automatically power down the transceiver only when automatic power-saving mode is selected. Disabled power saving must not leave the radio off after the beacon countdown.
- **JIT:** fold literals only when their memory is tracked for invalidation, and use the actual write mask when invalidating a block. Both ARM64 and x86_64 backends check whether a literal was registered.
- **Rendering:** skip unchanged compute-renderer configuration and stop generating/uploading edge data or compiling shaders for the inactive edge pass.
- **Optional networking API:** let a frontend provide hostname-to-IPv4 answers to the built-in DNS responder. The table is empty by default; ordinary resolver behavior is preserved.

### Integration

Companion Android PR: https://github.com/rafaelvcaetano/melonDS-android/pull/1682. The Android proposal pins this core revision. Merge the core first, then point the app's submodule at the accepted upstream commit if merging changes its SHA. The WFC settings screen edits firmware DNS settings and does not depend on the optional hostname API.

### Validation and limits

- The source tree is byte-for-byte identical to the previously reviewed core proposal; only contribution metadata was cleaned up.
- [Hosted Android integration build](https://github.com/Umberto-DEV/melonDS-android/actions/runs/40112578134) passed against this exact core revision: ARM64 APK compiled, 180 Android JVM tests passed, and the test APK/report artifacts were uploaded.
- Earlier ARM64 host validation covered sanitizers, synthetic JIT invalidation and DNS packet handling. Test harnesses are included in the companion Android proposal under `tools/host-tests/`; those host checks were not rerun for this metadata-only core resubmission.
- A prior paired Android build received five weeks of user testing on an AYN Thor. This is separate from testing newly added Android changes.
- The JIT/interpreter framebuffer comparison has a known discrepancy reproduced identically with the upstream and proposed cores. x86_64 runtime validation is still outstanding.

Supersedes #18, whose original source fork was removed. No emulation changes have been added during this resubmission.

issues.title: Enlarge SPU output ring buffer 2048 -> 8192
issues.body:
## What

Enlarges the SPU output ring buffer from 2048 to 8192 stereo samples (~43 ms → ~170 ms) in `InitOutput` (one-line change: the final doubling becomes an 8× step).

## Why

The ring is drained by the app's audio callback, once per callback period. With pitch-preserving fast-forward, the emulator produces `N × 48000` samples per real second (N = speed multiplier). At 8× the production between two callbacks (~3840 samples at a 480-frame callback) overran the old 2048-sample ring; the ring's overflow semantics drop the oldest samples, which is heard as crackling. 8192 covers the worst case (960-frame callbacks on power-saving devices: 384000 / (48000/960) = 7680) with margin.

This is the companion change to the app-side pitch-preservation feature; the app repository's pull request references it and updates the submodule pointer accordingly.

issues.title: Only set firmware paths when internal firmware is not used
issues.body:
When the user uses internal firmware without configuring external BIOS path, a crash can be observed when running a game:

```
pid: 3681, tid: 3971, name: RxCachedThreadS  >>> me.magnum.melonds.dev <<<
    01 pc 00000000004d2ae8  /data/app/~~usflvTWmCZy5aZBFXYAWbw==/me.magnum.melonds.dev-25PisQX1TquKFQM3tiMHeA==/lib/arm64/libmelonDS-lib.so (std::__ndk1::basic_string<char, std::__ndk1::char_traits<char>, std::__ndk1::allocator<char> >::assign(char const*)+32) (BuildId: e35bf127bac26d87c4586a7e22a1ca23e0a8e37d)
    02 pc 0000000000373400  /data/app/~~usflvTWmCZy5aZBFXYAWbw==/me.magnum.melonds.dev-25PisQX1TquKFQM3tiMHeA==/lib/arm64/libmelonDS-lib.so (MelonDSAndroid::setConfiguration(MelonDSAndroid::EmulatorConfiguration)+116) (BuildId: e35bf127bac26d87c4586a7e22a1ca23e0a8e37d)
    03 pc 000000000000d5b0  /data/app/~~usflvTWmCZy5aZBFXYAWbw==/me.magnum.melonds.dev-25PisQX1TquKFQM3tiMHeA==/lib/arm64/libmelonDS-android-frontend.so (Java_me_magnum_melonds_MelonEmulator_setupEmulator+260) (BuildId: 8a43c4a5b4f6d670c96f04b0c7ca13ff73987116)
```

Inspecting setConfiguration, it seems that the firmware paths are set regardless of whether internal firmware is used. The internal firmware shouldn't require these paths, and having them unset results in the crash detailed above.

To fix this, only set the paths when required. The check for internal firmware is sufficient for this purpose.

Test:
	1. Run a clean install of melonDS, without configuring BIOS and without enabling custom BIOS & firmware (internal firmware only)
	2. Initialise a known-affected game (Pokemon HG)
	3. The game runs without any crash observed
